label: The Bottom Line
headline: Growth is real, but onboarding capacity now caps how fast bookings convert to revenue

blocks.proof: ARR grew from $32M to $37M this quarter; enterprise new logos accounted for $4.2M of the $6.3M gross increase.
blocks.implication: Protect the enterprise motion before diversifying spend.

blocks.proof: Workflow adoption rose from 41% to 68% of accounts over three quarters.
blocks.implication: The product motion scales; the constraint has moved downstream.

blocks.claim: Onboarding capacity is now the limiter
blocks.proof: 14 signed accounts are queued for onboarding, more than double the prior quarter.
blocks.implication: Approve the two additional onboarding hires this quarter.

source: Illustrative data — replace with your own metrics.
notes: None of these three points stands alone: growth funds the case for more onboarding capacity, and the adoption curve is what proves the demand is durable rather than a one-quarter spike. The open question is timing, not direction.
